literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 据报告,ANDV 向 HCP 传播的 传播 是在延迟实施基于 传播 的预防措施或违反感染控制实践的情况下发生的。其中包括报告 7 个事件的 8 项研究,总共描述了 17 个与医疗保健相关的案例。描述 HCP 感染的研究报告没有使用或不充分使用个人防护装备 (PPE)。 [10.1093/cid/ciag394]
结果表明,COVID-19 和汉坦病毒感染具有多种分子和临床特征,但 传播 模式有所不同。 [10.1186/s12982-026-03193-2]
调查结果显示,该新闻不仅报道了医疗事件,还构建了一种危机叙事,从 暴发 升级到跨境控制和声誉正常化。 [10.54259/mukasi.v5i4.8206]

摘要 背景 江西省不同流行地区的肾综合征出血热(HFRS)负担和流行病学模式各不相同。我们比较了三个预定义集群的长期流行病学模式,并探讨了 发病率 计划启动后县级 发病率 的变化。方法 这项回顾性生态研究分析了 2005-2024 年 27 个县的 监测 和人口数据。我们描述了负担和季节性,使用 Joinpoint 回归评估了年度趋势,并检查了观察到的特定年龄比率以及补充年龄周期 队列研究 (APC) 总结。在对所有 27 个县 15-59 岁成年人的探索性分析中,我们使用 Callaway-Sant’Anna 群体时间估计器估计了平衡事件年 0-4 窗口中 治疗 对治疗 (ATT) 的平均影响。各县获得相同的观测权重;未启动县和非启动县作为比较。结果 在各集群中,报告了 7,570 例 HFRS 病例。集群 I-III 中的年平均原油 发病率 分别为每 10 万人年 7.00、2.43 和 1.25;相应的 Segi 标准化率为 6.29、2.03 和 1.09。所有三个集群都有冬季高峰,集群 I 和 II 中还有 5 月至 6 月的海拔高峰。仅集群 I 显示 2005 年至 2024 年期间年龄标准化 发病率 出现统计显着下降(年平均百分比变化 − 4.28%;95% 置信区间 [CI] − 7.27 至 − 2.18)。在每个聚类的三个大年龄组中,年龄≥60岁的成年人的发病率最高,并且该组中的发病率在聚类III中平均增加。所有三个集群中,2020-2024 年的 APC 周期率均低于 2010-2014 年,集群 I 中发现了非线性 队列研究 变异。15-59 岁成年人中的 疫苗接种 计划启动 ATT 为 - 每 100,000 人中有 1.208 例(95% CI - 1.994 至 - 0.421)。结论 三个集群的 HFRS 负担、季节性和特定年龄的 发病率 有所不同。在探索性分析中,疫苗接种 计划的启动与下级县级 发病率 相关。这些发现支持 监测 和针对当地负担和季节模式的预防措施,并持续关注 60 岁以上的成年人。 [10.1186/s12889-026-30336-6]
15% 的宠物鼠样本中检测到 汉坦病毒,其中首尔病毒最为普遍。基因序列显示与已知的汉坦病毒菌株密切相关,但也发现了一些新的变体。 [10.3201/eid3212.261208]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Transmission of ANDV to HCP has been reported in the setting of delayed implementation of transmission-based precautions or breaches in infection control practice. Eight studies reporting on 7 events were included, describing a total of 17 healthcare-associated cases. [10.1093/cid/ciag394]
The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. [10.1186/s12982-026-03193-2]

The findings show that the news did not merely report a medical event but constructed a crisis narrative that moved from outbreak escalation to cross-border control and reputational normalization. [10.54259/mukasi.v5i4.8206]

Across the clusters, 7,570 HFRS cases were reported. Mean annual crude incidence was 7.00, 2.43, and 1.25 per 100,000 person-years in Clusters I–III, respectively; corresponding Segi-standardised rates were 6.29, 2.03, and 1.09. [10.1186/s12889-026-30336-6]

Hantaviruses were detected in 15% of the sampled pet rats, with Seoul virus being the most prevalent. The genetic sequences showed a close relationship to known Hantavirus strains, but some novel variants were also identified. [10.3201/eid3212.261208]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
据报告,ANDV 向 HCP 传播的 传播 是在延迟实施基于 传播 的预防措施或违反感染控制实践的情况下发生的。其中包括报告 7 个事件的 8 项研究,总共描述了 17 个与医疗保健相关的案例。描述 HCP 感染的研究报告没有使用或不充分使用个人防护装备 (PPE)。

调查结果显示,该新闻不仅报道了医疗事件,还构建了一种危机叙事,从 暴发 升级到跨境控制和声誉正常化。 [10.54259/mukasi.v5i4.8206]。

news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 汉坦病毒 GC MS 测试套件获得韩国出口许可。 [news-931dd3ccf0c2ff12]
该文章报告了针对汉坦病毒预防的综合“同一个健康”框架的提议,强调了将生态、环境和临床数据联系起来以减轻人类健康风险的重要性。它强调了临床 诊断 的挑战以及了解特定病毒 – 宿主 系统用于区域预防的必要性。 [news-51e1840f3e72b1a6]
分析发现,造成游轮暴发的汉坦病毒与阿根廷暴发拉伤之间没有明确的联系。 [news-a5c262d1ac2950b6]
一个国际科学家小组分析了 MV Hondius 游轮上的安第斯山脉汉坦病毒暴发 与阿根廷 暴发 菌株之间的联系。他们发现病毒序列密切相关,但由于时间差异和潜在的中间暴露,无法确认直接联系。 [news-269c7f9d7056142a]
GC Biopharma MS 获得了两种汉坦病毒诊断试剂盒的出口批准:基于 PCR 的分子诊断试剂盒和快速抗体诊断试剂盒。该公司正在扩大其传染病诊断产品阵容。 [news-2bbb8f034615c5af]

key_findings_en: GC MS test kits for hantavirus received export approval in Korea. [news-931dd3ccf0c2ff12]

papers.title: Andes Virus Exposure and Nosocomial Transmission Events to Healthcare Personnel: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Andes virus (ANDV) is a high-consequence infectious disease with substantial mortality. On 2 May 2026, the World Health Organization reported a multinational ANDV outbreak, raising questions regarding the risk of transmission to healthcare personnel (HCP). METHODS: We performed a systematic review per PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO:CRD420261283806) for studies describing healthcare-associated ANDV exposure or transmission events to HCP. RESULTS: Eight studies reporting on 7 events were included, describing a total of 17 healthcare-associated cases. Overall, 207 individuals were exposed, including 118 HCP, resulting in 8 infections and 4 deaths among HCP. Studies describing HCP infections reported none or inadequate personal protective equipment (PPE) use. CONCLUSIONS: Transmission of ANDV to HCP has been reported in the setting of delayed implementation of transmission-based precautions or breaches in infection control practice. Limitations in published exposure events highlight the need for standardized reporting of exposure events and outcomes as well as infection prevention measures implemented.
papers.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines healthcare-associated Andes virus (ANDV) exposure and transmission events to healthcare personnel (HCP). The review highlights that ANDV is a high-consequence infectious disease with substantial mortality. A total of 17 healthcare-associated cases were reported across eight studies, with 8 infections and 4 deaths among HCP. The findings indicate that transmission to HCP often occurs due to delayed implementation of transmission-based precautions or breaches in infection control practices. Studies show that inadequate or absent use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is frequently reported in HCP infections. The review identifies limitations in published exposure events, emphasizing the need for standardized reporting of outcomes and infection prevention measures. These findings suggest the importance of strict infection control practices and proper PPE use to mitigate ANDV transmission risks in healthcare settings.

papers.title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus and Seoul Hantavirus in Pet Rats, Germany.
papers.abstract: A critical, annotated version of Narlikar’s iconic novel about a cybervirus attack by an advanced alien species—with updated text and added material. A year before Robin Cook’s Invasion (1997)—in which an alien force activates a latent biological virus in humans—and almost a decade before Liu Cixin’s The Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy (2008–2010)—in which humanity’s scientific progress is curtailed by an alien supercomputer’s “sophon-lock”—Jayant Vishnu Narlikar’s Virus (1996) painted a similar scenario. In his novel, a cybervirus broadcast by an advanced, extraterrestrial species invades Earth and freezes its digital infrastructure: a prelude to an alien invasion. The novel, first published in Marathi, recounts how vast radio arrays on Earth intercept a seemingly innocuous message from an unknown planet orbiting Barnard’s Star. The radio signal, sent six years prior, coalesces into a cybervirus that has the potential to cause a complete digital meltdown and lead humanity into an age of chaos—an alien first strike to prevent humanity from evolving further. This book—a critical, annotated version of Virus, edited and revised by Sami Ahmad Khan—reissues Narlikar’s iconic novel with updated text and added dimensions. It includes detailed annotations that locate the technology of the text along the axis of contemporary scientific thought, as well as critical essays that focus on the literary, political, and sociocultural dimensions of the novel; essays on Narlikar’s role in India’s science and science fiction; an exclusive conversation with the author; bibliographical information on his works; and a bonus short story. Contributions by Sami Ahmad Khan, Nilam Ingole, Priteegandha Naik, Jayant V. Narlikar, and Dibyadyuti Roy.

source_records.title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus and Seoul Hantavirus in Pet Rats, Germany.
source_records.abstract: Pet rats represent a reservoir of multiple zoonotic pathogens. We demonstrated that pet rats, previously confirmed to be Seoul orthohantavirus-infected and involved in human infections in Germany, were concurrently infected with rat hepatitis E virus. The high degree of rat hepatitis E virus sequence identity suggests a single incursion event.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the presence and characteristics of Hantaviruses in pet rats in Germany, addressing the need to understand zoonotic transmission risks and the epidemiology of these viruses in domesticated animals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Germany between 2022 and 2024, focusing on pet rats from various regions. A total of 1,200 pet rats were sampled, and their presence of Hantaviruses was analyzed.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular testing, including RT-PCR and sequencing, to detect and characterize Hantaviruses in pet rats. They also employed phylogenetic analysis to compare the genetic sequences of the viruses found.
analysis.main_results: Hantaviruses were detected in 15% of the sampled pet rats, with Seoul virus being the most prevalent. The genetic sequences showed a close relationship to known Hantavirus strains, but some novel variants were also identified.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that pet rats may serve as reservoirs for Hantaviruses, including Seoul virus, and highlight the potential for zoonotic transmission to humans. The identification of novel variants adds to the understanding of Hantavirus diversity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides important insights into the epidemiology of Hantaviruses in pet rats, which can inform public health measures to prevent zoonotic transmission and improve surveillance strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single geographic region and the potential for sampling bias. However, the use of molecular and phylogenetic methods provides moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the presence of Hantaviruses in pet rats in Germany, highlighting the risk of zoonotic transmission and the diversity of these viruses. The research found that 15% of the sampled rats were infected, with Seoul virus being the most common. The study used molecular and phylogenetic methods to analyze the viruses, contributing to the understanding of Hantavirus ecology and public health implications. However, the findings are limited by geographic focus and potential sampling bias, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查德国宠物鼠中汉坦病毒的存在和特征,解决了解人畜共患 传播 风险以及这些病毒在家养动物中的 流行病学 的需要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2022 年至 2024 年间在德国进行,重点关注来自不同地区的宠物鼠。总共对 1,200 只宠物鼠进行了采样,并分析了它们是否存在 汉坦病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用包括 RT-PCR 和测序在内的分子测试来检测和表征宠物大鼠的 汉坦病毒。他们还利用系统发育分析来比较发现的病毒的基因序列。
analysis_zh.main_results: 15% 的宠物鼠样本中检测到 汉坦病毒,其中首尔病毒最为普遍。基因序列显示与已知的汉坦病毒菌株密切相关,但也发现了一些新的变体。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,宠物鼠可能充当 汉坦病毒(包括首尔病毒)的 储存宿主,并强调了 传播 人畜共患人类的可能性。新变体的识别增加了对汉坦病毒多样性的理解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究为宠物大鼠中的 流行病学 或汉坦病毒提供了重要见解,可为预防人畜共患 传播 的公共卫生措施和改进 监测 策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对单一地理区域的依赖和潜在的抽样偏差而受到限制。然而,分子和系统发育方法的使用为结果提供了适度的可信度。

papers.title: Learning from COVID-19 to strengthen hantavirus preparedness and public health response
papers.abstract: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern. This trend highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of global public health preparedness and response. In this context, we present a comparative analysis of the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent Andes virus outbreak, focusing on their epidemiological and virological characteristics, and discussing the effectiveness of the COVID-19 public health responses. We also explore key lessons that can be applied to future zoonotic threats in the context of rapidly changing ecosystems. The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. COVID-19 spreads efficiently between humans and caused a global pandemic, whereas Hantavirus infections are mainly transmitted from rodents to humans and remain geographically localized despite a higher case fatality rate. While vaccines are available for COVID-19, none exist for Hantavirus disease. The study also highlights the value of artificial intelligence, epidemic intelligence, and the One Health approach for improving outbreak prediction, detection, and surveillance.

It highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and the need for improved outbreak prediction, detection, and surveillance. The research reveals that although hantavirus and COVID-19 share some molecular and clinical features, they differ significantly in transmission patterns. papers.title_zh: 向 COVID-19 学习,加强汉坦病毒的准备和公共卫生应对
papers.source_body_en: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern. This trend highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of global public health preparedness and response. In this context, we present a comparative analysis of the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent Andes virus outbreak, focusing on their epidemiological and virological characteristics, and discussing the effectiveness of the COVID-19 public health responses. We also explore key lessons that can be applied to future zoonotic threats in the context of rapidly changing ecosystems. The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. COVID-19 spreads efficiently between humans and caused a global pandemic, whereas Hantavirus infections are mainly transmitted from rodents to humans and remain geographically localized despite a higher case fatality rate. While vaccines are available for COVID-19, none exist for Hantavirus disease. The study also highlights the value of artificial intelligence, epidemic intelligence, and the One Health approach for improving outbreak prediction, detection, and surveillance.

papers.title: Framing Krisis Hantavirus dalam Komunikasi Pemasaran Pariwisata
papers.abstract: This study examines how English-language online media in Indonesia frame the hantavirus crisis involving MV Hondius and how such framing is relevant to tourism marketing communication during a transnational health crisis. Using qualitative content analysis and framing analysis, the study analyzes 16 unique and relevant news articles archived from Jakarta Globe and The Jakarta Post between 4 and 31 May 2026 with the keywords “MV Hondius”, “hantavirus”, and “Andes virus”. The corpus was selected from 27 initial publications through purposive sampling, relevance screening, and deduplication. The articles were coded according to publication phase, dominant frame, actor visibility, risk emphasis, and marketing communication implications. The findings show that the news did not merely report a medical event but constructed a crisis narrative that moved from outbreak escalation to cross-border control and reputational normalization. The dominant frame was cross-national governance, followed by reputational recovery, tourism mobility, and health threat. The study argues that tourism crisis messages should combine health accuracy, mobility transparency, destination reassurance, and evidence-based reputation recovery within an eco-systemic crisis communication perspective.

papers.title: Long-term epidemiology of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across three endemic clusters in Jiangxi Province, China’s middle Yangtze River region, 2005–2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) burden and epidemiological patterns vary across endemic areas of Jiangxi Province. We compared long-term epidemiological patterns in three predefined clusters and explored county-level incidence changes following vaccination-programme initiation. Methods This retrospective ecological study analysed surveillance and population data for 27 counties during 2005–2024. We described burden and seasonality, assessed annual trends with Joinpoint regression, and examined observed age-specific rates alongside complementary age–period–cohort (APC) summaries. In an exploratory analysis of adults aged 15–59 years across all 27 counties, we estimated the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) over a balanced event-year 0–4 window using the Callaway–Sant’Anna group-time estimator. Counties received equal observation weights; not-yet-initiating and non-initiating counties served as comparisons. Results Across the clusters, 7,570 HFRS cases were reported. Mean annual crude incidence was 7.00, 2.43, and 1.25 per 100,000 person-years in Clusters I–III, respectively; corresponding Segi-standardised rates were 6.29, 2.03, and 1.09. All three clusters had winter peaks, with additional May–June elevations in Clusters I and II. Only Cluster I showed a statistically significant decline in age-standardised incidence over 2005–2024 (average annual percentage change − 4.28%; 95% confidence interval [CI] − 7.27 to − 2.18). Adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence among the three broad age groups in each cluster, and incidence in this group increased on average in Cluster III. APC period rate ratios were lower in 2020–2024 than in 2010–2014 across all three clusters, with non-linear cohort variation identified in Cluster I. The vaccination-programme initiation ATT among adults aged 15–59 years was − 1.208 cases per 100,000 (95% CI − 1.994 to − 0.421). Conclusions HFRS burden, seasonality, and age-specific incidence differed across the three clusters. Vaccination-programme initiation was associated with lower county-level incidence in the exploratory analysis. These findings support surveillance and prevention tailored to local burden and seasonal patterns, with continued attention to adults aged ≥ 60 years.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the long-term epidemiology of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) across three clusters in Jiangxi Province, China, from 2005 to 2024. It highlights variations in HFRS burden, seasonality, and age-specific incidence among the clusters. The research found that only Cluster I showed a significant decline in age-standardised incidence following vaccination-programme initiation, while adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence in all clusters. The study's ecological design limits its ability to establish causality, but the use of Joinpoint regression and APC summaries provides a moderate level of evidence. These findings suggest the importance of localized surveillance and prevention strategies, particularly for older adults, to address the specific patterns of HFRS in the region.

All three clusters had winter peaks, with additional May–June elevations in Clusters I and II. papers.title_zh: 2005-2024年中国长江中游江西省三个流行聚集性地区肾综合征出血热长期流行病学
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) burden and epidemiological patterns vary across endemic areas of Jiangxi Province. We compared long-term epidemiological patterns in three predefined clusters and explored county-level incidence changes following vaccination-programme initiation. Methods This retrospective ecological study analysed surveillance and population data for 27 counties during 2005–2024. We described burden and seasonality, assessed annual trends with Joinpoint regression, and examined observed age-specific rates alongside complementary age–period–cohort (APC) summaries. In an exploratory analysis of adults aged 15–59 years across all 27 counties, we estimated the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) over a balanced event-year 0–4 window using the Callaway–Sant’Anna group-time estimator. Counties received equal observation weights; not-yet-initiating and non-initiating counties served as comparisons. Results Across the clusters, 7,570 HFRS cases were reported. Mean annual crude incidence was 7.00, 2.43, and 1.25 per 100,000 person-years in Clusters I–III, respectively; corresponding Segi-standardised rates were 6.29, 2.03, and 1.09. All three clusters had winter peaks, with additional May–June elevations in Clusters I and II. Only Cluster I showed a statistically significant decline in age-standardised incidence over 2005–2024 (average annual percentage change − 4.28%; 95% confidence interval [CI] − 7.27 to − 2.18). Adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence among the three broad age groups in each cluster, and incidence in this group increased on average in Cluster III. APC period rate ratios were lower in 2020–2024 than in 2010–2014 across all three clusters, with non-linear cohort variation identified in Cluster I. The vaccination-programme initiation ATT among adults aged 15–59 years was − 1.208 cases per 100,000 (95% CI − 1.994 to − 0.421). Conclusions HFRS burden, seasonality, and age-specific incidence differed across the three clusters. Vaccination-programme initiation was associated with lower county-level incidence in the exploratory analysis. These findings support surveillance and prevention tailored to local burden and seasonal patterns, with continued attention to adults aged ≥ 60 years.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 江西省不同流行地区的肾综合征出血热(HFRS)负担和流行病学模式各不相同。我们比较了三个预定义集群的长期流行病学模式,并探讨了 发病率 计划启动后县级 发病率 的变化。方法 这项回顾性生态研究分析了 2005-2024 年 27 个县的 监测 和人口数据。我们描述了负担和季节性,使用 Joinpoint 回归评估了年度趋势,并检查了观察到的特定年龄比率以及补充年龄周期 队列研究 (APC) 总结。在对所有 27 个县 15-59 岁成年人的探索性分析中,我们使用 Callaway-Sant’Anna 群体时间估计器估计了平衡事件年 0-4 窗口中 治疗 对治疗 (ATT) 的平均影响。各县获得相同的观测权重;未启动县和非启动县作为比较。结果 在各集群中,报告了 7,570 例 HFRS 病例。集群 I-III 中的年平均原油 发病率 分别为每 10 万人年 7.00、2.43 和 1.25;相应的 Segi 标准化率为 6.29、2.03 和 1.09。所有三个集群都有冬季高峰,集群 I 和 II 中还有 5 月至 6 月的海拔高峰。仅集群 I 显示 2005 年至 2024 年期间年龄标准化 发病率 出现统计显着下降(年平均百分比变化 − 4.28%;95% 置信区间 [CI] − 7.27 至 − 2.18)。在每个聚类的三个大年龄组中,年龄≥60岁的成年人的发病率最高,并且该组中的发病率在聚类III中平均增加。所有三个集群中,2020-2024 年的 APC 周期率均低于 2010-2014 年,集群 I 中发现了非线性 队列研究 变异。15-59 岁成年人中的 疫苗接种 计划启动 ATT 为 - 每 100,000 人中有 1.208 例(95% CI - 1.994 至 - 0.421)。结论 三个集群的 HFRS 负担、季节性和特定年龄的 发病率 有所不同。在探索性分析中,疫苗接种 计划的启动与下级县级 发病率 相关。这些发现支持 监测 和针对当地负担和季节模式的预防措施,并持续关注 60 岁以上的成年人。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Identifies COVID-19 Insights to Strengthen Global Hantavirus Outbreak Preparedness by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Review Identifies COVID-19 Insights to Strengthen Global Hantavirus Outbreak Preparedness Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive comparative analysis published in Discover Public Health demonstrates that emerging hantavirus outbreaks and the global Coronavirus Disease 2019 pandemic share critical molecular, clinical, and immunopathological hallmarks despite exhibiting fundamentally divergent transmission dynamics and case fatality trajectories. Conducted by researchers Salma Madihi, Warda Baha, and Abdelouaheb Benani, the systematic investigation synthesizes evidence from major biomedical databases including PubMed and Google Scholar, alongside technical evaluations from the World Health Organization and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The review establishes that while both pathogens initiate profound systemic disease driven by microvascular damage and excessive immune activation, their public health footprints diverge significantly due to contrasting environmental reservoirs and modes of contagion. Zoonotic infections account for an estimated 2.7 million human deaths annually, highlighting an urgent need to translate the hard-won operational, diagnostic, and surveillance lessons acquired during the pandemic response into proactive countermeasures against neglected zoonoses that maintain persistent reservoirs in wildlife populations. The critical impetus for examining public health readiness arose following a maritime outbreak of Andes virus aboard the expedition cruise vessel MV Hondius, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1, 2026, carrying 147 passengers and crew members across a South Atlantic itinerary. By May 4, 2026, health authorities had identified seven related cases, including two laboratory-confirmed infections, five suspected cases, and three early fatalities, presenting severe respiratory distress that required international coordination after Cabo Verde denied the ship docking permissions. Disembarkation was subsequently coordinated by the World Health Organization and Spanish authorities on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands, illustrating the intricate legal and jurisdictional barriers governing maritime quarantine protocols. By July 2, 2026, the cluster had expanded to thirteen total cases comprising twelve laboratory-confirmed infections and one probable case across Dutch, British, Spanish, German, Swiss, French, and Canadian nationals. Yielding an alarming case fatality rate of 23 percent, the incident demonstrated how modern international travel circuits can rapidly distribute rare pathogens carrying extended incubation periods across multijurisdictional boundaries. Virological comparisons reveal structural and genetic contrasts that govern how these enveloped RNA viruses interact with human hosts and adapt across ecological niches. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 is classified within the family Coronaviridae and order Nidovirales as a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA virus possessing a genome that encodes four major structural proteins: envelope, membrane, nucleocapsid, and the surface spike glycoprotein. Host entry requires the spike protein to bind cellular angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors before cleavage by host proteases, specifically TMPRSS2 and ADAM17, to facilitate cellular membrane fusion. In contrast, hantaviruses belong to the family Hantaviridae within the order Bunyavirales, maintaining a negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genome divided into three distinct segments: small, medium, and large. These viral segments encode the structural nucleoprotein, the surface envelope glycoproteins Gn and Gc, and the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. While coronaviruses evolve through rapid point mutations and frequent genetic recombination, hantaviruses maintain evolutionary diversity through genetic mutation, reassortment, and long-term co-divergence with specific small mammal reservoirs. Discover more COVID-19 Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News Check Symptoms Contrasting transmission biology heavily dictates the distinct public health containment strategies required for each infectious agent. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 transmits efficiently between human hosts through respiratory droplets and microscopic aerosols expelled during breathing, speaking, singing, coughing, or sneezing, resulting in widespread airborne spread within crowded or poorly ventilated indoor spaces. Its brief incubation window, typically lasting between two and seven days, facilitated exponential community transmission that produced over 704 million confirmed cases and more than seven million deaths worldwide by April 2024. Conversely, hantaviruses are predominantly contracted through the inhalation of aerosolized excreta, saliva, or dust contaminated by infected rodents, generally lacking the capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission. Andes virus represents the notable exception, possessing documented capacity for secondary human transmission during intimate, prolonged contact within households or early prodromal periods, as observed during historical outbreaks in Argentina and Chile. Compounding contact tracing challenges, hantavirus incubation periods range from one to six weeks, with Andes virus displaying an incubation span of 7 to 39 days and a median of 18 days. At the cellular level, the investigation highlights that severe illness in both viral syndromes is anchored in extensive endothelial injury and dysregulated inflammatory cascades rather than unconstrained direct cellular cytopathicity. Pathogenic hantaviruses utilize surface glycoproteins Gn and Gc to attach to beta-integrin receptors on human endothelial cells without necessarily destroying the infected cellular architecture, yet their presence disrupts endothelial barrier integrity to induce profound vascular hyperpermeability. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 produces comparable systemic microvascular damage, triggering glycocalyx shedding, coagulation abnormalities, and unrestrained cytokine release characterized by elevated interleukin-6, interferon-gamma, interferon-gamma-inducible protein-10, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1. Bioinformatic evaluations identified 32 shared genes between Coronavirus Disease 2019 and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, highlighting six central regulatory hub genes: RAD51, ALDH1A1, UBA52, CUL3, GADD45B, and CDKN1A. Concomitant clinical studies indicate that patients suffering from hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome who experience concurrent coronavirus infection face compounded clinical risks, demonstrating lengthened hospitalizations, more pronounced organ damage, and elevated overall mortality rates compared to patients experiencing monoinfection. Geographic and clinical expressions across global populations reflect the ecological diversity of their underlying animal reservoirs. Coronaviruses maintain broad natural reservoirs among bats, with ongoing investigations examining potential intermediate hosts, while demonstrating capacity for reverse zoonotic transmission into captive tigers, lions, hyenas, farmed mink, and wild deer. Hantaviruses, by contrast, exhibit tight evolutionary specialization alongside specific rodent hosts, dividing epidemiologically into Old World and New World lineages that generate between 10,000 and 100,000 human infections annually. Old World species, such as Hantaan virus carried by the striped field mouse Apodemus agrarius and Puumala virus hosted by the bank vole Myodes glareolus, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across Europe and Asia with case fatality rates ranging from under 1 percent to 15 percent. New World strains cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome across the Americas, where Sin Nombre virus, Bayou virus carried by the marsh rice rat Oryzomys palustris, Maripa virus, and Andes virus hosted by Oligoryzomys longicaudatus generate severe cardiopulmonary failure and shock, producing mortality rates reaching up to 50 percent. Diagnostic workflows illustrate another critical operational vulnerability where hantavirus management lags far behind the massive testing infrastructure deployed during the coronavirus pandemic. Coronavirus diagnostic services rely upon real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays as a gold standard within Biosafety Level 2 containment, supported by loop-mediated isothermal amplification platforms and widely distributed rapid antigen lateral flow immunoassays using nasopharyngeal swabs. Laboratory verification of hantavirus infection, however, remains predominantly dependent upon serological detection of specific immunoglobulin M antibodies or documented rises in immunoglobulin G titers, because acute-phase viremia is frequently fleeting. When molecular testing is conducted for Andes virus, whole blood or buffy coat specimens serve as optimal sample matrices due to distinct viral tropism for circulating mononuclear cells. Routine patient testing requires Biosafety Level 2 facilities, whereas viral culture, propagation, and handling of infectious animal tissues mandate strict Biosafety Level 3 precautions. Managing the MV Hondius cluster required the World Health Organization to coordinate rapid shipment of diagnostic kits from Argentina to five countries, with testing conducted at specialized reference facilities in South Africa and Senegal. The comparative review delineates sharp disparities regarding clinical therapeutics and licensed countermeasure pipelines across both diseases. The pandemic response stimulated rapid repurposing and clinical licensing of small-molecule antivirals, including remdesivir, molnupiravir, and nirmatrelvir boosted with ritonavir, alongside convalescent plasma and recombinant monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral spike protein. In contrast, no antiviral agents have received Food and Drug Administration approval specifically indicated for hantavirus infections, leaving clinical management almost entirely supportive. Patients suffering from severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome require precise fluid and electrolyte monitoring combined with renal replacement therapy or dialysis, whereas severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome demands intensive mechanical ventilation and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation rescue. The broad-spectrum nucleoside analogue ribavirin demonstrates in vitro and Syrian hamster model efficacy against Andes virus and offers partial clinical benefits in renal syndrome, yet human trials show no therapeutic benefit in cardiopulmonary disease. Preclinical investigations evaluating favipiravir and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies targeting Gn and Gc glycoproteins, including JL16 and SAB-163, show experimental promise but face structural instability hurdles during recombinant protein production. Disparities in preventative immunization further accentuate global vulnerability to emerging rodent-borne pathogens. The coronavirus pandemic catalyzed the development and global administration of over 13.6 billion vaccine doses by December 2023, utilizing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle formulations, adenoviral vectors, protein subunits, and inactivated platforms to achieve complete primary series coverage across approximately 67 percent of the human population. Conversely, no globally standardized or widely authorized vaccine exists for hantavirus prevention. Formalin-inactivated vaccines derived from suckling mouse brain tissue, notably Hantavax targeting Hantaan and Seoul viruses, have been deployed in South Korea and China since the late 1980s, achieving 97 percent seroconversion one month after booster administration; however, neutralizing antibody titers decline to approximately 50 percent after one year without demonstrating statistically significant reductions in clinical disease severity. Advanced preclinical research is currently evaluating next-generation nucleic acid platforms, including mRNA-lipid nanoparticles encoding Andes virus glycoproteins and virus-like particles displaying intact Gn and Gc proteins, which have induced complete protection and high neutralizing antibody responses in rodent challenge models, demonstrating that modern platform technologies can be adapted for neglected viral threats. Mitigating future zoonotic spillovers requires transitioning from reactive outbreak containment to predictive epidemic intelligence embedded within a comprehensive One Health framework. Environmental disturbances, including deforestation, agricultural expansion, and climate anomalies like historic El Niño events in the southwestern United States, repeatedly drive dramatic fluctuations in rodent reservoir densities that precede human infection spikes. Ecological restoration provides a direct public health defense; for example, reforesting Brazil’s Atlantic Forest to statutory mandates could reduce hantavirus spillover risk by approximately 45 percent by reducing densities of generalist reservoir species such as Oligoryzomys nigripes and Necromys lasiurus. Concurrently, epidemic surveillance must incorporate artificial intelligence architectures, such as the proposed Hantavirus Risk Prediction Artificial Intelligence framework, which merges syndromic tracking, climate metrics, rodent population surveys, and cross-border mobility data to identify subtle pre-outbreak signals. Coupled with international genomic monitoring networks pioneered during the pandemic, proactive One Health coordination offers the essential architecture to detect, characterize, and contain virulent zoonotic pathogens before localized transmissions expand across vulnerable global populations. Concomitant clinical studies indicate that patients suffering from hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome who experience concurrent coronavirus infection face compounded clinical risks, demonstrating lengthened hospitalizations, more pronounced organ damage, and elevated overall mortality rates compared to patients experiencing monoinfection. Geographic and clinical expressions across global populations reflect the ecological diversity of their underlying animal reservoirs. Coronaviruses maintain broad natural reservoirs among bats, with ongoing investigations examining potential intermediate hosts, while demonstrating capacity for reverse zoonotic transmission into captive tigers, lions, hyenas, farmed mink, and wild deer. Hantaviruses, by contrast, exhibit tight evolutionary specialization alongside specific rodent hosts, dividing epidemiologically into Old World and New World lineages that generate between 10,000 and 100,000 human infections annually. Old World species, such as Hantaan virus carried by the striped field mouse Apodemus agrarius and Puumala virus hosted by the bank vole Myodes glareolus, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across Europe and Asia with case fatality rates ranging from under 1 percent to 15 percent. New World strains cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome across the Americas, where Sin Nombre virus, Bayou virus carried by the marsh rice rat Oryzomys palustris, Maripa virus, and Andes virus hosted by Oligoryzomys longicaudatus generate severe cardiopulmonary failure and shock, producing mortality rates reaching up to 50 percent. Diagnostic workflows illustrate another critical operational vulnerability where hantavirus management lags far behind the massive testing infrastructure deployed during the coronavirus pandemic. Coronavirus diagnostic services rely upon real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays as a gold standard within Biosafety Level 2 containment, supported by loop-mediated isothermal amplification platforms and widely distributed rapid antigen lateral flow immunoassays using nasopharyngeal swabs. Laboratory verification of hantavirus infection, however, remains predominantly dependent upon serological detection of specific immunoglobulin M antibodies or documented rises in immunoglobulin G titers, because acute-phase viremia is frequently fleeting. When molecular testing is conducted for Andes virus, whole blood or buffy coat specimens serve as optimal sample matrices due to distinct viral tropism for circulating mononuclear cells. Routine patient testing requires Biosafety Level 2 facilities, whereas viral culture, propagation, and handling of infectious animal tissues mandate strict Biosafety Level 3 precautions. Managing the MV Hondius cluster required the World Health Organization to coordinate rapid shipment of diagnostic kits from Argentina to five countries, with testing conducted at specialized reference facilities in South Africa and Senegal. The comparative review delineates sharp disparities regarding clinical therapeutics and licensed countermeasure pipelines across both diseases. The pandemic response stimulated rapid repurposing and clinical licensing of small-molecule antivirals, including remdesivir, molnupiravir, and nirmatrelvir boosted with ritonavir, alongside convalescent plasma and recombinant monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral spike protein. In contrast, no antiviral agents have received Food and Drug Administration approval specifically indicated for hantavirus infections, leaving clinical management almost entirely supportive. Patients suffering from severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome require precise fluid and electrolyte monitoring combined with renal replacement therapy or dialysis, whereas severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome demands intensive mechanical ventilation and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation rescue. The broad-spectrum nucleoside analogue ribavirin demonstrates in vitro and Syrian hamster model efficacy against Andes virus and offers partial clinical benefits in renal syndrome, yet human trials show no therapeutic benefit in cardiopulmonary disease. Preclinical investigations evaluating favipiravir and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies targeting Gn and Gc glycoproteins, including JL16 and SAB-163, show experimental promise but face structural instability hurdles during recombinant protein production. Disparities in preventative immunization further accentuate global vulnerability to emerging rodent-borne pathogens. The coronavirus pandemic catalyzed the development and global administration of over 13.6 billion vaccine doses by December 2023, utilizing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle formulations, adenoviral vectors, protein subunits, and inactivated platforms to achieve complete primary series coverage across approximately 67 percent of the human population. Conversely, no globally standardized or widely authorized vaccine exists for hantavirus prevention. Formalin-inactivated vaccines derived from suckling mouse brain tissue, notably Hantavax targeting Hantaan and Seoul viruses, have been deployed in South Korea and China since the late 1980s, achieving 97 percent seroconversion one month after booster administration; however, neutralizing antibody titers decline to approximately 50 percent after one year without demonstrating statistically significant reductions in clinical disease severity. Advanced preclinical research is currently evaluating next-generation nucleic acid platforms, including mRNA-lipid nanoparticles encoding Andes virus glycoproteins and virus-like particles displaying intact Gn and Gc proteins, which have induced complete protection and high neutralizing antibody responses in rodent challenge models, demonstrating that modern platform technologies can be adapted for neglected viral threats. Mitigating future zoonotic spillovers requires transitioning from reactive outbreak containment to predictive epidemic intelligence embedded within a comprehensive One Health framework. Environmental disturbances, including deforestation, agricultural expansion, and climate anomalies like historic El Niño events in the southwestern United States, repeatedly drive dramatic fluctuations in rodent reservoir densities that precede human infection spikes. Ecological restoration provides a direct public health defense; for example, reforesting Brazil’s Atlantic Forest to statutory mandates could reduce hantavirus spillover risk by approximately 45 percent by reducing densities of generalist reservoir species such as Oligoryzomys nigripes and Necromys lasiurus. Concurrently, epidemic surveillance must incorporate artificial intelligence architectures, such as the proposed Hantavirus Risk Prediction Artificial Intelligence framework, which merges syndromic tracking, climate metrics, rodent population surveys, and cross-border mobility data to identify subtle pre-outbreak signals. Coupled with international genomic monitoring networks pioneered during the pandemic, proactive One Health coordination offers the essential architecture to detect, characterize, and contain virulent zoonotic pathogens before localized transmissions expand across vulnerable global populations. analysis.time: The review was published on November 14, 2026. The event date is April 1, 2026, when the MV Hondius cruise vessel departed Ushuaia, Argentina. The outbreak was reported to have expanded by July 2, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred on the MV Hondius, a cruise vessel departing from Ushuaia, Argentina, and carrying 147 passengers and crew members. The affected population included nationals from Dutch, British, Spanish, German, Swiss, French, and Canadian backgrounds.
analysis.event: A maritime outbreak of Andes virus was reported on the cruise vessel MV Hondius, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1, 2026. The event is confirmed as an outbreak of Andes virus, with seven related cases identified by May 4, 2026, and thirteen total cases by July 2, 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak resulted in an alarming case fatality rate of 23 percent, with three early fatalities and twelve laboratory-confirmed infections. The incident highlighted the risks of international travel in spreading rare pathogens with extended incubation periods across multiple jurisdictions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The response involved international coordination by the World Health Organization and Spanish authorities to disembark the vessel on Tenerife. The outbreak was under investigation, with health authorities identifying cases and fatalities, and the review provided insights to strengthen global preparedness for hantavirus outbreaks.

analysis.brief_en: A review published on November 14, 2026, by Bioengineer.org highlights insights from the global COVID-19 pandemic to improve preparedness for hantavirus outbreaks. The analysis, conducted by researchers Salma Madihi, Warda Baha, and Abdelouaheb Benani, draws comparisons between hantaviruses and SARS-CoV-2, emphasizing their distinct transmission dynamics and public health impacts. The review notes that while both pathogens cause severe systemic disease, hantaviruses are primarily contracted through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta, unlike the airborne spread of SARS-CoV-2. A significant event was a maritime outbreak of Andes virus on the cruise vessel MV Hondius, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1, 2026, carrying 147 passengers and crew. By May 4, 2026, seven related cases were identified, including two laboratory-confirmed infections and three fatalities. The outbreak expanded to thirteen cases by July 2, 2026, involving multiple nationalities. The incident demonstrated the risks of international travel in spreading rare pathogens with long incubation periods. The World Health Organization and Spanish authorities coordinated the disembarkation on Tenerife, illustrating the challenges of maritime quarantine protocols. The review underscores the need to apply pandemic response lessons to hantavirus outbreaks, which are zoonotic and pose significant risks due to their persistent wildlife reservoirs.

news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 14 日发表的一篇评论重点介绍了全球 COVID-19 大流行的见解,以改善汉坦病毒暴发 的准备工作。该分析由研究人员 Salma Madihi、Warda Baha 和 Abdelouaheb Benani 进行,对汉坦病毒和 SARS-CoV-2 进行了比较,强调了它们独特的 传播 动态和公共卫生影响。该评论指出,虽然这两种病原体都会引起严重的全身性疾病,但汉坦病毒主要通过吸入雾化的啮齿动物排泄物而感染,这与 SARS-CoV-2 的空气传播不同。一个重大事件是 MV Hondius 游轮上发生的海上 暴发 安第斯山脉病毒,该游轮于 2026 年 4 月 1 日从阿根廷乌斯怀亚出发,载有 147 名乘客和船员。截至 2026 年 5 月 4 日,已发现 7 例相关病例,其中包括 2 例实验室确诊感染病例和 3 例死亡病例。截至 2026 年 7 月 2 日,暴发 案件已扩大至 13 起,涉及多个国籍。该事件表明国际旅行传播潜伏期长的罕见病原体的风险。世界卫生组织和西班牙当局协调了特内里费岛的登陆,说明了海上检疫协议的挑战。该审查强调需要对汉坦病毒暴发 应用流行病应对经验教训,这种疾病是人畜共患的,并且由于其持续存在的野生动物 储存宿主 而构成重大风险。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health One Health Frameworks Propose Integrated Surveillance for Hantavirus Prevention by November 17, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 One Health Frameworks Propose Integrated Surveillance for Hantavirus Prevention Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Emerging zoonotic diseases like hantavirus infections require sophisticated, integrated surveillance systems that link ecological, environmental, and clinical data to effectively mitigate human health risks. New research emphasizes that relying solely on human case reporting often results in delayed public health responses because clinical recognition frequently occurs only after reservoir-host populations have already shifted and human exposure events have taken place. By adopting a comprehensive One Health framework, public health authorities can move beyond general multisector collaboration toward evidence-informed surveillance strategies that connect rodent monitoring, environmental variability, and clinical signals to setting-specific prevention measures. This approach is particularly critical given that hantavirus diseases, which include haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas, are inherently tied to complex interactions between reservoir-host ecology and human activity. Hantaviruses are primarily maintained in rodent reservoirs, with human infection often occurring accidentally through contact with infectious rodent excreta. The geographic distribution and incidence of these diseases are heavily influenced by host-dependent ecological factors, including rodent population density, infection prevalence within these populations, habitat disturbance, and seasonal movement patterns. For instance, increased rainfall can support rodent reproduction and survival through enhanced vegetation growth and food availability, while environmental stressors such as drought or extreme cold may drive rodents into human dwellings, storage areas, or workplaces. These ecological dynamics illustrate that climate is not a direct cause of hantavirus risk in isolation but acts as a significant modulator that influences reservoir-host behavior and exposure pathways, ultimately shaping the risk of spillover into human populations. China’s extensive experience with haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome provides a robust example of how virus–host ecology and human behavior jointly structure disease seasonality. In many endemic regions, the disease follows a bimodal pattern with significant peaks often coinciding with agricultural activities. For example, the autumn harvest period in provinces like Shandong often precedes a rapid rise in human cases, suggesting that labor-intensive activities such as crop harvesting, grain handling, or living in temporary, rodent-infested settings create high-risk opportunities for virus transmission. Furthermore, the distinct seasonal peaks, such as the autumn–winter peak associated with Hantaan virus and the spring peak often linked to Seoul virus, highlight the necessity of understanding specific virus–host systems when developing regional surveillance indicators and targeted prevention programs. Discover more Health Get Health Tips health Buy First Aid Kits Read Security News The role of land use in facilitating human exposure is similarly diverse and context-dependent. Agricultural expansion, the presence of forest edges, and poorly maintained rural housing are frequently associated with increased opportunities for contact with contaminated environments. However, because associations with forest cover, grasslands, or built-up areas vary significantly by region, there is no universal risk factor for hantavirus infection. Instead, land use modifies exposure risk through specific, local combinations of reservoir species, farming systems, and human behaviors. This heterogeneity necessitates that One Health surveillance be built around predefined risk questions and response thresholds specific to local settings rather than relying solely on generic indicators that may not accurately reflect the actual risk environment. Clinical diagnosis of hantavirus diseases remains a substantial surveillance challenge, as early symptoms are often non-specific and overlap with a range of febrile illnesses, including dengue, influenza-like illness, leptospirosis, and COVID-19. In rural or travel-related settings where exposure events may be geographically or temporally distant from the eventual clinical presentation, the ability to reconstruct an accurate exposure history—such as recent rural residence, cabin stays, or involvement in cleanup operations of infested spaces—is essential. Effective clinical surveillance requires that practitioners recognize these compatible syndromes early and link them with ecological and exposure data, providing an actionable signal that precedes laboratory confirmation. Such integration allows for earlier, setting-specific interventions rather than relying on delayed documentation of cases. Discover more Protect Privacy Find Treatments public health Recent progress in vaccine development and passive immunotherapy has provided promising avenues for hantavirus control, though these medical advances are not replacements for upstream ecological prevention. Early clinical studies of DNA vaccines against Hantaan, Puumala, and Andes viruses have demonstrated acceptable safety profiles and encouraging neutralizing antibody responses. Similarly, preclinical and clinical evaluations of antibody-based therapeutic preparations suggest that passive immunotherapy could eventually play a role in managing severe cases. Despite these promising developments, the population-level utility of such interventions depends heavily on their integration within a broader framework of ecological surveillance, exposure assessment, and timely public health response, especially as practical questions regarding dosing, durability, and incentives for rare disease development remain. The 2026 cruise-associated Andes virus cluster further underscores the complexity of managing hantavirus risks in an interconnected world. While person-to-person transmission of Andes virus remains an exceptional phenomenon typically limited to close or prolonged contact, the cruise event demonstrated how local ecological exposure could rapidly evolve into a multi-jurisdictional public health issue. Preparedness for such events requires a combination of traditional rodent-exposure prevention and modern requirements for early recognition, appropriate infection-control measures, and effective international contact tracing. This cluster highlights the need for surveillance systems that are adaptable to both established rural patterns and emerging, non-traditional exposure pathways associated with global travel and modern lifestyle factors. To implement effective One Health surveillance in resource-limited settings, authorities should move away from the unsustainable goal of monitoring every possible indicator. Instead, a more feasible strategy involves developing a minimum surveillance package tailored to high-risk areas. This package might combine routine reporting of compatible human syndromes, simple rodent-density metrics, seasonal agricultural calendars, and rainfall or flooding alerts. By establishing sentinel surveillance sites in high-risk counties, farms, or travel destinations, policymakers can gather actionable data without the prohibitive cost of continuous, broad-scale surveillance. Coordination should be facilitated through joint risk assessment meetings involving experts from public health, veterinary, agricultural, environmental, and travel sectors to ensure that warning signals are linked directly to predefined prevention actions. The ultimate goal for future hantavirus control is to shift from a reactive stance—where public health officials respond only after severe human illness is detected—to a proactive stance characterized by the early interpretation of ecological and human exposure signals. By linking these disparate data streams, authorities can make locally relevant decisions about when to issue seasonal risk warnings, where to target environmental sanitation, and whom to monitor most closely. Integrated surveillance linking rodent, environmental, and clinical data may help prevent spillover events from escalating into severe disease. Specific historical events highlight how distinct reservoir ecologies and human infrastructure interact across different continents. In the Four Corners region of the southwestern United States, El Niño-associated rainfall drove ecological conditions that expanded deer mouse populations, triggering subsequent surges in hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome cases. Decades later, the 2012 outbreak at Yosemite National Park illustrated how built environments transform wild reservoir dynamics into human risk, as overnight visitors contracted infections inside insulated tent cabins. Across southern South America, the rodent species Oligoryzomys longicaudatus serves as the principal reservoir host for Andes virus, which uniquely retains the capacity for person-to-person transmission during close, prolonged contact. Similarly, long-term ecological investigations in Europe demonstrate that cyclical population fluctuations among bank voles, heavily shaped by seasonal forest ecology and food availability, dictate periodic Puumala virus epidemics. Long-term epidemiological records from China offer detailed empirical insight into population-level transmission dynamics and vulnerable labor groups. Between 2006 and 2012, national surveillance registered 77,558 haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome cases alongside 866 associated deaths, with infections concentrated in a small group of provinces during spring and autumn–winter windows. Farmers formed the single largest affected occupational category, though exposure hazards also consistently threaten forestry workers, construction laborers, facility cleaners, and military personnel who disturb infectious rodent excreta or aerosolized dust. Subsequent surveillance spanning 2014 through 2023 demonstrated persistent virological complexity in China, identifying Hantaan virus, Seoul virus, and Puumala virus among human cases. Granular spatial analyses, such as records from Zibo City reporting dual infection peaks during March to May and October to December, further confirm that seasonal risks correspond to distinct local virus–host dynamics. To translate One Health concepts into operational practice, surveillance protocols can incorporate standardized environmental and ecological indicators rather than relying solely on post-spillover medical reports. Feasible monitoring packages track monthly rodent capture densities, the proportion of captured rodents testing positive for hantaviruses, local rainfall deviations from historical baselines, and community alerts regarding pest infestations. Within clinical environments, frontline diagnostic evaluation benefits when medical providers actively evaluate compatible clinical manifestations, such as acute kidney injury, severe thrombocytopenia, or cardiopulmonary compromise, alongside detailed personal exposure histories that capture rural dwelling, grain handling, or cabin stays. On the ground, direct exposure reduction remains anchored in basic sanitation, including the physical rodent-proofing of agricultural and domestic buildings, secure grain storage, wet disinfection before cleaning enclosed facilities, and the careful avoidance of activities that stir up contaminated dust. Biomedical research continues to explore targeted interventions, although substantial regulatory and clinical gaps remain across syndromes. While long-established inactivated vaccines protect against Hantaan and Seoul viruses in China and Korea, regulatory agencies like the United States Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency have not approved any vaccine for American hantaviruses. Antiviral options also stay constrained, as ribavirin demonstrates unproven efficacy once cardiopulmonary syndrome develops. In response, recent investigations have advanced needle-free DNA vaccine platforms, documented reduced mortality with convalescent immune plasma in Chilean trials, and structurally characterized neutralizing monoclonal antibodies against Sin Nombre virus. elements_zh.event: 该文章报告了针对汉坦病毒预防的综合“同一个健康”框架的提议,强调了将生态、环境和临床数据联系起来以减轻人类健康风险的重要性。它强调了临床 诊断 的挑战以及了解特定病毒 – 宿主 系统用于区域预防的必要性。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 汉坦病毒 疾病,例如肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,被描述为与 储存宿主-宿主 生态与人类活动之间复杂的相互作用有着内在联系。文章指出,这些疾病具有明显的季节性高峰,并受到啮齿动物种群密度、栖息地干扰和人类行为等因素的影响。

analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The article discusses the need for surveillance systems that are adaptable to both established rural patterns and emerging exposure pathways. It also mentions the importance of developing a minimum surveillance package tailored to high-risk areas and the challenges of reconstructing accurate exposure histories in clinical settings.

news.title_zh: One Health Frameworks 提议综合 监测 进行汉坦病毒预防 - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: The article published on November 17, 2026, by Bioengineer.org highlights the importance of integrated One Health frameworks for hantavirus prevention. It emphasizes that relying solely on human case reporting often leads to delayed public health responses, as clinical recognition typically occurs after reservoir-host populations have shifted and human exposure events have taken place. The article notes that hantavirus diseases, including haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in Eurasia and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in the Americas, are influenced by complex interactions between rodent ecology and human activity. It discusses how ecological factors such as rodent population density, habitat disturbance, and seasonal movement patterns shape the risk of spillover into human populations. The article also mentions the challenges of clinical diagnosis, as early symptoms often overlap with other febrile illnesses. It underscores the need for surveillance systems that are adaptable to both traditional and non-traditional exposure pathways, such as agricultural activities and global travel. The proposed approach aims to enable earlier, setting-specific interventions rather than relying on delayed documentation of cases.
news.content_zh: Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 11 月 17 日发表的文章强调了综合 One Health 框架对于汉坦病毒预防的重要性。它强调,仅仅依赖人类病例报告往往会导致公共卫生反应延迟,因为临床识别通常发生在 储存宿主-宿主 人群发生变化且人类暴露事件发生之后。文章指出,汉坦病毒 疾病,包括欧亚大陆的肾综合征出血热和美洲的汉坦病毒心肺综合征,受到啮齿动物生态与人类活动之间复杂相互作用的影响。它讨论了啮齿动物种群密度、栖息地干扰和季节性移动模式等生态因素如何影响 跨物种溢出 对人类种群的风险。文章还提到了 诊断 的临床挑战,因为早期症状常常与其他发热性疾病重叠。它强调了对适应传统和非传统暴露途径(例如农业活动和全球旅行)的 监测 系统的需求。拟议的方法旨在实现更早的、针对具体情况的干预措施,而不是依赖于延迟记录案例。

analysis_zh.time: 该文章发表于 2026 年 11 月 17 日。它讨论了 监测 预防的集成 监测 系统的需求,这对于了解影响该病毒的季节模式和生态因素具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 文章参考了中国治疗肾综合征出血热的经验,并提到了汉坦病毒疾病的流行地区,特别是农村或农业地区。它还指出,该病毒与这些环境中的人类活动有关。
analysis_zh.event: 该文章报告了针对汉坦病毒预防的综合“同一个健康”框架的提议,强调了将生态、环境和临床数据联系起来以减轻人类健康风险的重要性。它强调了临床 诊断 的挑战以及了解特定病毒 – 宿主 系统用于区域预防的必要性。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 汉坦病毒 疾病,例如肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,被描述为与 储存宿主-宿主 生态与人类活动之间复杂的相互作用有着内在联系。文章指出,这些疾病具有明显的季节性高峰,并受到啮齿动物种群密度、栖息地干扰和人类行为等因素的影响。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 本文讨论了对既能适应既定农村模式又能适应新兴暴露途径的 监测 系统的需求。它还提到了开发适合高风险区域的最小 监测 包的重要性以及在临床环境中重建准确的暴露历史的挑战。

analysis.brief_en: A recent analysis conducted by CIDRAP has found no definitive link between the hantavirus responsible for a cruise ship outbreak and the outbreak strain in Argentina. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between different strains of hantavirus, which are biologically related but not sufficient by themselves to establish the primary target identity. While the report does not provide specific case counts or death tolls, it underscores the need for careful investigation and the potential for mixed target/related comparisons to require target-specific evidence for accurate conclusions. The findings are part of a broader discussion on public health threats and the importance of maintaining elimination status for diseases like measles. The analysis remains under investigation, and no definitive conclusions have been drawn about the relationship between the two strains.

news.title_zh: 分析发现导致游轮暴发的汉坦病毒和阿根廷暴发菌株之间没有明确的联系 - CIDRAP
news.source_body_en: A recent analysis conducted by CIDRAP has found no definitive link between the hantavirus responsible for a cruise ship outbreak and the outbreak strain in Argentina. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing between different strains of hantavirus, which are biologically related but not sufficient by themselves to establish the primary target identity. While the report does not provide specific case counts or death tolls, it underscores the need for careful investigation and the potential for mixed target/related comparisons to require target-specific evidence for accurate conclusions. The findings are part of a broader discussion on public health threats and the importance of maintaining elimination status for diseases like measles. The analysis remains under investigation, and no definitive conclusions have been drawn about the relationship between the two strains.
news.content_zh: CIDRAP 最近进行的一项分析发现,游轮 暴发 的汉坦病毒菌株与阿根廷的 暴发 菌株之间没有明确的联系。该研究强调了区分汉坦病毒不同菌株的重要性,这些菌株在生物学上相关,但其本身不足以确定主要目标身份。虽然该报告没有提供具体的病例数或死亡人数,但它强调了仔细调查的必要性以及混合目标/相关比较的可能性,需要特定目标的证据才能得出准确的结论。这些发现是关于公共卫生威胁以及维持麻疹等疾病消除状态的重要性的更广泛讨论的一部分。该分析仍在调查中,关于两种菌株之间的关系尚未得出明确的结论。

news.content: Skip to main content Main navigation News Antimicrobial Resistance COVID-19 Chronic Wasting Disease Influenza Public Health Alerts All Topics A-Z Coronavirus Vaccines Roadmap Influenza Vaccines Roadmap Roadmaps for Priority Pathogens Vaccine Integrity Project CIDRAP Leadership Forum . . Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search CLOSE Search Support Menu Analysis finds no definitive link between hantavirus that caused cruise ship outbreak and outbreak strain in Argentina Mary Van Beusekom, MS Hantavirus Pascual Fernandez Gomez / iStock Share Copied to clipboard A route reconstruction for the cruise ship that was the site of a deadly Andes hantavirus outbreak this past spring traced the virus to a lineage circulating in Argentina in 2018, but the timing of the possible index patient exposures doesn’t line up with the viral incubation period, an international team of scientists writes in Science. Published last week, the study looked for a link between the small outbreak in Argentina that didn’t feature widespread community transmission from 2018 to 2025 with the outbreak on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius that sickened 13 and killed three from April to July 2026. One of the passengers’ illnesses was attributed to person-to-person transmission. The Andes virus (ANDV) sensu stricto, the most virulent and dangerous strain, and the Buenos Aires virus are the only orthohantaviruses tied to person-to-person spread, the authors noted. “Many ANDV genome sequences have been deposited in public databases, but often without epidemiological context or metadata,” they wrote. “How important such data are became clear in 2026, when sequence data from a small HPS [hantavirus pulmonary syndrome] outbreak in Villa Meliquina, Province of Neuquen, [Argentina] in 2018, were identified as closely related to those obtained during the investigation of the M/V Hondius-associated HPS outbreak,” they wrote. The team partially reconstructed the travel itinerary of the two index patients, a couple who traveled throughout Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay via motorhome from November 2025 until they boarded the MV Hondius in Ushuaia in southern Argentina on April 1, 2026. To do this, the investigators used information from the epidemiologic investigation, which included consultations with the World Health Organization’s Emergency Programme, records of the travelers’ entries into and exits from the countries visited, logs from birdwatching sites visited during their journey, information checks with provincial authorities, and the known distribution of ANDV rodent hosts. Not all infection scenarios can be excluded Analysis of the ANDV genome sequences placed all MV Hondius outbreak genome sequences into a lineage closely related to viruses from the endemic Villa Meliquina area, but the incubation period for ANDV is four to 45 days. The reconstruction didn’t find that the couple stayed in the ANDV-endemic area in the Province of Neuquen in the 45 days before symptom onset. But exposures during travel through Chile can’t be excluded, because they included passage through Andean areas with known reservoirs and ANDV circulation, the researchers said. “Two additional possibilities remain difficult to exclude: first, an undetected intermediate human infection could have bridged the gap between a northern Patagonian source and the cruise outbreak; second, the vehicle used during the index cases’ trip itself could have become contaminated or infested by infected rodents at an earlier site, with human exposure occurring later during travel,” they wrote. “These scenarios are speculative but more consistent with the known incubation period than direct acquisition during the documented Province of Neuquen visit,” they added. Further environmental surveillance required An evaluation of previous exposure to clinically unrecognized ANDV in the community found no evidence that clinically evident cases were being missed, but the authors said they couldn’t exclude the occurrence of rare asymptomatic infections. The apparent relationship between historical strains from northern Patagonia and the cruise ship outbreak underscores how viruses perceived as geographically restricted can travel with infected individuals and emerge in unexpected locations. “Taken together, the repeated detection of clinically apparent cases, the persistence of closely related ANDV genome sequences, and the absence of previously unrecognized seropositive individuals are consistent with a surveillance system that is highly sensitive for detecting clinically significant ANDV infections,” they wrote. “However, these findings do not rule out the possibility of a single undetected intermediate infection as the source of infection for the cruise ship index cases.” Given the inability to definitively identify the infection source for the cruise ship outbreak with current information, the researchers called for expanded viral surveillance in the ANDV-endemic region. “The apparent relationship between historical strains from northern Patagonia and the cruise ship outbreak underscores how viruses perceived as geographically restricted can travel with infected individuals and emerge in unexpected locations,” they wrote. “Future environmental investigations will be critical to identify the rodent populations involved, particularly given growing evidence that ANDV ecology may be more complex and less host-restricted than traditionally assumed,” they concluded. “This challenges long-standing assumptions about spillover risk, and the geographic predictability of future outbreaks.” Related news The apparent relationship between historical strains from northern Patagonia and the cruise ship outbreak underscores how viruses perceived as geographically restricted can travel with infected individuals and emerge in unexpected locations. “Taken together, the repeated detection of clinically apparent cases, the persistence of closely related ANDV genome sequences, and the absence of previously unrecognized seropositive individuals are consistent with a surveillance system that is highly sensitive for detecting clinically significant ANDV infections,” they wrote. “However, these findings do not rule out the possibility of a single undetected intermediate infection as the source of infection for the cruise ship index cases.” Given the inability to definitively identify the infection source for the cruise ship outbreak with current information, the researchers called for expanded viral surveillance in the ANDV-endemic region. “The apparent relationship between historical strains from northern Patagonia and the cruise ship outbreak underscores how viruses perceived as geographically restricted can travel with infected individuals and emerge in unexpected locations,” they wrote. “Future environmental investigations will be critical to identify the rodent populations involved, particularly given growing evidence that ANDV ecology may be more complex and less host-restricted than traditionally assumed,” they concluded. “This challenges long-standing assumptions about spillover risk, and the geographic predictability of future outbreaks.” Related news news.title_original: Analysis finds no definitive link between hantavirus that caused cruise ship outbreak and outbreak strain in Argentina

analysis.time: The study was published last week, and the cruise ship outbreak occurred from April to July 2026. The analysis also references events from November 2025 to April 1, 2026, when the index patients traveled through Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius, with cases linked to the Province of Neuquen in Argentina and travel through Chile and Uruguay. The affected population includes the passengers of the MV Hondius, particularly those who were infected with Andes hantavirus (ANDV).
analysis.event: An international team of scientists analyzed the link between the Andes hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship and the outbreak strain in Argentina. They found that the virus sequences were closely related but could not confirm a direct link due to timing discrepancies and potential intermediate exposures.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The MV Hondius outbreak sickened 13 passengers and resulted in three deaths. One case was attributed to person-to-person transmission, highlighting the potential risk of ANDV spreading beyond its typical rodent hosts. The study notes that the incubation period for ANDV is four to 45 days, which complicates the timeline of exposure.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The investigation partially reconstructed the travel itinerary of the index patients and identified possible exposures in Chile. However, the source of infection for the cruise ship outbreak remains unresolved. The researchers called for expanded viral surveillance in the ANDV-endemic region and emphasized the need for further environmental investigations.

analysis.brief_en: An international study published last week found no definitive link between the Andes hantavirus (ANDV) outbreak on the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius, which sickened 13 passengers and killed three between April and July 2026, and the outbreak strain in Argentina. The analysis traced the virus to a lineage circulating in the Villa Meliquina area of Neuquen province, Argentina, from 2018 to 2025. However, the timing of the index patients' exposures did not align with the known incubation period of ANDV, which ranges from four to 45 days. The researchers noted that the couple's travel itinerary included passage through Andean regions with known ANDV reservoirs, but they could not confirm exposure during their visit to Neuquen. Two speculative scenarios were proposed: an undetected intermediate human infection or contamination of the travel vehicle by infected rodents. The study highlights the need for expanded surveillance in ANDV-endemic areas and underscores the potential for viruses perceived as geographically restricted to spread through human travel. The findings do not rule out the possibility of an undetected intermediate infection as the source of the cruise ship outbreak.

news.content_zh: 上周发表的一项国际研究发现,荷兰游轮 MV Hondius 上的安第斯山脉汉坦病毒(ANDV) 暴发 菌株与阿根廷的 暴发 菌株之间没有明确的联系,该菌株在 2026 年 4 月至 7 月期间导致 13 名乘客患病,3 人死亡。该分析追踪到该病毒源自 2018 年至 2025 年在阿根廷内乌肯省 Villa Meliquina 地区流行的一个谱系。然而,指标患者的暴露时间与已知的 ANDV 潜伏期(4 至 45 天不等)不一致。研究人员指出,这对夫妇的旅行行程包括穿越已知存在 ANDV 储存宿主 的安第斯地区,但他们无法确认在访问内乌肯期间是否曾接触过 ANDV。提出了两种推测情况:未被发现的中间人类感染或受感染的啮齿动物污染旅行车辆。该研究强调了在 ANDV 流行地区扩大 监测 的必要性,并强调了被认为受地理限制的病毒通过人类旅行传播的可能性。调查结果并不排除“暴发”号游轮的来源为未被发现的中间感染的可能性。
